items.title: The two halves of trust: Why DPDP compliance is more than a legal puzzle
items.summary: Imagine commissioning a state-of-the-art skyscraper. The architect delivers a brilliant blueprint: a design that is elegant, compliant with all building codes, and visionary in its scope. The legal team ensures all contracts are sound and permits are in order. But without an engineer to translate those plans into structural realities, without a construction crew to pour the foundation and erect the steel, the blueprint remains just that: a brilliant but unrealized idea. As India embarks on its journey to full DPDP Act compliance, many organizations find themselves in a similar position. They have the legal blueprint, meticulously crafted by expert counsel. They understand the articles of the law, the definitions, and the penalties. Yet, the chasm between understanding the law and implementing it on the ground remains vast. The notification of the DPDP Rules has started an 18-month countdown, and closing this gap has become the most pressing challenge for businesses and the legal professionals who guide them. Delhi High Court refuses to stop private channel from broadcasting Gurbani from Golden Temple
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday refused to pass any interim orders on a plea filed by Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) to stop a private television channel from broadcasting or rebroadcasting Gurbani (sacred hymns and scriptures of Sikhism) from the Golden Temple. SGPC and a channel named PTC approached the High Court against Galactic Television and Communications alleging copyright infringement. SGPC – the apex body entrusted with managing the Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib) – argued that they hold the copyright in the broadcast of the Gurbani from the Golden Temple. It stated that Galactic Television, by broadcasting the same, although with a 10-second delay, is violating their rights. At present, the Gurbani from the Golden Temple is broadcast on SGPC’s YouTube channel and on PTC. Justice Anup Jairam Bhambhani today gave a prima facie opinion that the Guru Granth Sahib is a literary work and that if its broadcast by SGPC is used for a genuine religious ceremony without resorting to commercialisation, it may not amount to copyright infringement. “It is a literary cum musical work. items.title: Supreme Court quashes FIRs against Samay Raina, 4 other comedians over remarks about disabled persons
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday quashed criminal cases filed against YouTuber-comedian Samay Raina and four other comedians over insensitive remarks made on the show India's Got Latent about persons with disabilities. A Bench Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana passed the order. Apart from Raina, the others who have been given relief in connection with this case are Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar alias Sonali Aditya Desai, and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The Court today appreciated the efforts made by Raina, Goyal, Ghai, Thakkar and Tanwar to organise shows for the benefit of persons with disabilities. " Once there are genuine efforts positive results are bound to be there. They are very bright youngsters. If they have started working in positive direction, there will be positive output," the Bench said. The Court proceeded to quash criminal cases filed against them over insensitve remarks against disabled persons. A Division Bench of Justice T Amarnath Goud and Justice S Datta Purkayastha was hearing two petitions seeking quashing of FIRs registered at East Agartala and West Agartala police stations under Sections 356 of the BNS (defamation) and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act (publishing obscene material online). The Court held that at the quashing stage, its task is confined to examining whether the FIR and charge-sheet prima facie disclose the ingredients of an offence. It cannot conduct a mini-trial or assess whether the allegations would ultimately hold up at trial. It found that the petitioner's statements had prima facie drawn criticism of the Prime Minister and the Mayor by mocking their names, and had hurt religious sentiment connected to Mata Tripureshwari. items.title: Allahabad High Court rejects woman’s plea seeking maternity leave for fourth child
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court recently dismissed a plea filed by a woman government employee seeking six months' maternity leave for her fourth child [Sashi Kumari v. State of UP and Others] Justice Manju Rani Chauhan passed the order on August 7 in a petition challenging a June 19 order by the government authorities who had rejected her claim for maternity leave for her fourth child. The petitioner argued that she had not availed maternity leave when her first three children were born and was therefore, entitled to the benefit for the fourth child since she was seeking maternity leave for the first time. The State opposed the plea, relying on the provisions of the Financial Handbook. It submitted that she was not entitled to maternity leave for her fourth child. Justice Manju Rani Chauhan The provision states that maternity leave is available to permanent or temporary women government employees for two occasions. It further provides that where a woman government employee has two or more living children, maternity leave cannot be granted.
